description: Create the frontend in frontend/ as a static-exported Next.js SPA (output: 'export', client-side rendered) served via CloudFront + S3. Registration and login both initiate the Cognito Managed Login hosted redirect to Google using OAuth2 Authorization Code + PKCE (no in-app username/password form). After login, the app holds the tokens client-side and shows a single button that calls the protected /hello endpoint through CloudFront (/api/*) and prints the response. Depends on FEAT-001 (Cognito domain, client id, CloudFront /api/* behavior) and FEAT-002 (hello route path).
steps: Create frontend/package.json with next, react, react-dom and scripts (dev, build, lint). Use Next.js app or pages router; keep it minimal SPA.
frontend/next.config.js: set output: 'export' (static export to out/), images.unoptimized true, and any basePath needed. Confirm it produces a fully static site with no SSR/Lambda@Edge.

frontend/lib/auth.ts: implement Authorization Code + PKCE against Cognito Managed Login. Generate code_verifier/code_challenge, redirect the browser to https://<cognito-domain>/oauth2/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<clientId>&redirect_uri=<appUrl>&scope=openid+email+profile&identity_provider=Google&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256. Handle the redirect back: exchange the code at https://<cognito-domain>/oauth2/token (public client, no secret, with code_verifier) for tokens; store the access/id token in memory or sessionStorage. Provide login(), register() (both trigger the same hosted redirect; register may pass a prompt/param but Google-only means both start the hosted flow), and logout() hitting the Cognito /logout endpoint.

Config: read Cognito domain, client id, region, and API base URL from public runtime config (e.g., NEXT_PUBLIC_ env vars baked at build, or a /config.json fetched at runtime so the same static build works across deploys). Document that these come from infra outputs. API base URL is '/api' (same-origin via CloudFront).

frontend/app (or pages): a single page. If not authenticated show 'Login with Google' and 'Register with Google' buttons that call login()/register(). A callback route/handler processes the ?code= redirect. When authenticated show a 'Call /hello' button that fetches `${apiBase}/hello` (i.e. /api/hello through CloudFront) with Authorization: Bearer <token> and prints the response text on the page.

Ensure the API path aligns with FEAT-001 CloudFront '/api/*' behavior and FEAT-002 backend route so that a call to /api/hello reaches the backend hello handler and returns 'Hello World'. Document the exact path mapping.

frontend/README.md: how to install (npm ci), run dev, build the static export (npm run build -> out/), the required NEXT_PUBLIC_/config values sourced from infra outputs, and how the PKCE Managed Login flow works.
acceptance_criteria: `npm ci && npm run build` in frontend/ succeeds and produces a static export in frontend/out/ with an index.html (no server runtime required).

The auth module builds the Cognito Managed Login authorize URL with response_type=code, code_challenge_method=S256, identity_provider=Google, and the configured scopes; there is no in-app username/password form.
The authenticated view has a single button that calls the /hello endpoint via /api and renders the returned response.
Cognito domain, client id, and API base are read from configuration (not hardcoded per-deploy), and the README documents which infra outputs supply them.
next lint / tsc passes (no type or lint errors that fail the build).
verification: Run `cd frontend && npm ci && npm run build` and confirm it exits 0 and frontend/out/index.html exists.
Run `cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit` (if TypeScript) and/or `npm run lint` and confirm no errors.
findings: Implemented frontend/ as a static-exported Next.js SPA (App Router, client-side only). next.config.js sets output:'export', images.unoptimized:true, trailingSlash:true; no SSR/Lambda@Edge. lib/auth.ts implements OAuth2 Authorization Code + PKCE entirely client-side using Web Crypto (crypto.getRandomValues + crypto.subtle SHA-256, base64url): login() and register() both call the same beginHostedRedirect() to https://<cognitoDomain>/oauth2/authorize with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri=origin+'/', scope='openid email profile', identity_provider=Google, code_challenge=S256(verifier), code_challenge_method=S256. handleRedirectCallback() exchanges ?code= at /oauth2/token (grant_type=authorization_code, public client, no secret, code_verifier) and stores tokens in sessionStorage; logout() clears tokens and hits /logout. There is no username/password form. app/page.tsx: unauthenticated shows 'Login with Google' + 'Register with Google'; authenticated shows a single 'Call /hello' button that fetches ${apiBase}/hello (i.e. /api/hello same-origin via CloudFront) with Authorization: Bearer <accessToken> and renders the response, plus a Log out button. Config is runtime (lib/config.ts fetches /config.json with NEXT_PUBLIC_ fallbacks): cognitoDomain<-auth CognitoDomainUrl, clientId<-auth UserPoolClientId, region<-us-east-1, apiBase='/api'; site origin (redirect_uri root) maps to storage AppUrl. Sample public/config.json ships with placeholders. redirect_uri uses origin+'/' to match auth.yaml CallbackURLs (${AppUrl}/ and ${AppUrl}/index.html) and LogoutURL. Verification on Node v22.23.2: npm install + npm run build succeed, producing out/index.html and out/config.json; npx tsc --noEmit clean; npm run lint (next lint) reports no warnings or errors. Pinned next@15.5.25 + eslint-config-next@15.5.25 (backport line) to avoid the 15.5.4 CVE; remaining npm-audit advisories are transitive Next.js build tooling (postcss/sharp/eslint plugin-kit), not runtime-exploitable in a static export (images unoptimized, no server). package-lock.json committed; node_modules/, out/, .next/ gitignored.
review_fixes: Review 2026-09-12-185023 BLOCKING (Issue 1, frontend/lib untracked) fixed: the root .gitignore was the stock GitHub Python template whose unanchored `lib/` rule (and `build/`, `dist/`, `lib64/`, `target/`, etc.) matched frontend/lib/, so frontend/lib/auth.ts and frontend/lib/config.ts (the OAuth2+PKCE flow and runtime config that app/page.tsx imports via @/lib/auth) were silently excluded and a fresh clone failed npm run build. Anchored those Python packaging build-dir rules to the repo root (/lib/, /lib64/, /build/, /dist/, /target/, etc.) so they only match top-level Python build output, kept __pycache__/ and .venv protections, added an explicit Node/Next.js section (node_modules/, .next/, frontend/out/, next-env.d.ts, *.tsbuildinfo), and git add'd both frontend/lib TypeScript files. Verified: git check-ignore -v frontend/lib/auth.ts returns nothing; git ls-files frontend/lib/ lists both .ts files; build outputs (.next, out, node_modules, next-env.d.ts, tsbuildinfo, __pycache__, .venv) remain ignored. No other intended source under backend/ or frontend/ is ignored. (Issue 5, token choice) added a code comment on callHello in frontend/lib/auth.ts documenting access-token vs id-token intent per endpoint; no behavior change (still sends the access token to /hello). Frontend re-verified on Node v22.23.2: npm ci, npx tsc --noEmit (clean), npm run lint (No ESLint warnings or errors), npm run build produced out/index.html.
